messages:
sarah.chen: Heads-up — a couple of large mobile customers on sdk-v1 are sending newline-delimited JSON frames (NDJSON) and fail to parse the new event-stream framing from v3. Errors in prod: JSON.parse on first chunk.
mitchell: ack. any sample requests?
sarah.chen: pasted an example from logs: `POST /v3/generate` body is a single stream where each line is `\n`-separated JSON. Content-Type: application/json; streaming client uses chunked newlines.
aj: that matches old mobile lib behavior. v3 uses `text/event-stream` style chunks and SSE-ish framing.
zane: what's breaking — payload shape or framing?
sarah.chen: framing. client expects each newline to be a complete JSON document, so partial frame from v3 -> parse error.
keisha: can we ask customers to bump SDK? Might be tough — one is a slow-release bank app.
mitchell: two options: 1) force a client-side SDK update (slow), 2) add a translation shim at the edge that converts v3 event frames -> NDJSON lines.
aj: 2 seems pragmatic short-term. But we should avoid implicit translation that hides server contract bugs. Prefer opt-in per-tenant flag.
zane: implementation idea: lightweight edge filter that buffers event-frame tokens until a logical message complete, then emit `\n`-delimited JSON. Very low CPU if we do it as streaming state machine. Could be a small Wasm module.
keisha: +1 on tenant opt-in. Add telemetry for translated messages so we can see how many customers rely on it. Also TTL for the flag (auto-expire in 90 days) to force migration.
sarah.chen: agree. Also need to preserve function-calling events and structured metadata. Example mapping: `event: message\ndata: {"id":123,"text":"..."}\n\n` -> `{"id":123,"text":"..."}\n`
mitchell: tradeoffs: adds CPU at edge, potential latency delta (ms) for buffering until newline boundary. But likely negligible for mobile payloads. Need performance tests.
aj: telemetry: emit `compat.ndjson_shim.v1` with tenant_id, per-message count, avg latency. Obfuscate PII.
zane: rollout plan suggestion: 1) build wasm shim + unit tests, 2) deploy to staging cluster behind feature flag, 3) enable for single tenant as canary, 4) monitor telemetry (errors, latency), 5) open migration ticket with customer.
keisha: ops constraints: we should gate on `X-Tenant-Compat: ndjson` header as well as tenant flag — allows client to signal intent and simplifies debugging.
mitchell: about retries/fallback: if shim fails, we should return 415 vs silently downgrade. Fail-fast helps surface misconfigurations.
sarah.chen: code sketch for header negotiation: ```if request.headers['X-Tenant-Compat']=='ndjson' || tenant.flags.ndjson_shim { route to ndjson-shim } else { normal v3 handling }```
aj: also add per-tenant rate limits for shim path to avoid noisy tenants hogging edge transforms.
zane: ops note: Wasm risk is small; still add a circuit-breaker (fallback to normal path + 502) if mem/cpu spike.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: new canary key created: canary/ndjson-shim. Staging cluster deployment window available Wed 03:00 UTC.
keisha: scheduling: let's aim for RFC follow-up doc that captures API contract, telemetry schema, opt-in lifecycle, and rollback plan. I can draft.
sarah.chen: action items: @zane prototype wasm shim (ETA 5d), @aj telemetry + event schema, @keisha RFC + rollout runbook, @mitchell perf bench on staging. I'll open tenant opt-in tickets for the two customers.
mitchell: sounds good. one more: add a short-lived debug mode that logs original frame IDs for tracing with customer consent.
aj: +1. privacy review note: require explicit consent for logging payloads.
keisha: will coordinate with security and legal.
sarah.chen: thanks all — will follow up with RFC link in this thread. :thumbsup:
